title: Fats Navarro and Cannonball
summary: Navarro's tone, a planned suite, and his Tampa roots.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What -- that reminds me, because Chino Pozo recorded with Fats Navarro. Did you ever play with Fats Navarro?
Oh, yeah, great trumpet player. I'm sorry when he died. Certainly a great trumpet player. We was rehearsing for a new album (inaudible) when he died.
He struck me as being particularly good at playing (blending in) (inaudible).

You know what? The guy was so -- he had such a big tone, that it was hard to find another trumpet player to be able to sit down next to him. And (in other words) (inaudible) get a trumpet player to sit down beside a man, you have to -- you have to go and pick it up and find -- go (inaudible) trumpet player, not just jazz trumpet player.

The third thing happen to this guy, it was (inaudible) me too at the same time he got killed. The guys used to play (inaudible) trumpet with the (inaudible) with Tom Mirosso (phonetic), big, fat guy. What was the name? (Inaudible).

He was -- we were rehearsing a suite somebody from California wrote for me, and those two guys are there. This guy was playing lead jazz (inaudible) and Navarro's supposed to play solos. Navarro was -- as you say, was a mechanical Dizzy Gillespie.

When I say mechanical, I don't mean exactly mechanical. In order to sample the difference between one and the other one, Dizzy was (inaudible) and Navarro can take the same solo, huh, and (inaudible) and play (inaudible).
So he would have taken a technical (inaudible).
He was a mechanical trumpet player (inaudible) the best. (Inaudible).

It's been suggested that he did Javarro (phonetic) -- I think it was Javarro, one of the numbers he played with Chino Posto -- but anyway, one of the numbers that he did play with Chino Posto that he had more understanding of Afro-Cuban rhythms than most jazz trumpeters in the early days because he came from deep South Florida.
And he's part Cuban, I think.

He's in local band -- yeah, he's in local band (inaudible). Yeah, yeah, he's -- same thing with Cannonball. He from down the same town. Cannonball, he never heard me, never played with me. And the day he came in there, we were recording (inaudible) he sat down. He say, (inaudible) tell me when I got to play. Gone -- no (inaudible).
